executive_bullets.title: Corvus wins BC Ferries Summit Class — 40 MWh across 4 vessels
executive_bullets.body: Corvus Energy awarded contract for four hybrid-electric double-ended ferries for BC Ferries. 10 MWh Dolphin NxtGen Power per vessel; architecture pre-wired for 70 MWh total. Built at China Merchants Weihai; ABB as integrator. First delivery 2029.

executive_bullets.title: Meyer Werft Project Vision — world first 82,000 GT battery-electric cruise concept
executive_bullets.body: Unveiled at Seatrade Cruise Global. 275m, 1856 pax, Corvus named as battery supplier. Up to 95% GHG reduction claimed. No contract yet — but signals cruise segment seriously considering battery-electric at scale for the first time.

supplier_moves.strategic_meaning: North American ferry dominance confirmed; future-ready 70 MWh architecture is a new commercial differentiator

supplier_moves.update: Gotland Horizon X 780 kWh hybrid catamaran
supplier_moves.strategic_meaning: Winning Nordic ferry routes previously held by Corvus; 20-yr battery life a key differentiator

market_signals.label: Signal 1 — Ferry market has tipped to mainstream
market_signals.observation: Corvus won BC Ferries, CMAL, Washington State and Matson within 12 months. Multi-vessel programmes are now the norm.
market_signals.interpretation: Ferry electrification is no longer early-adopter. Shipyards are standardising on battery-electric for new fleet programmes. Structural shift.

market_signals.label: Signal 2 — Cruise segment entering the picture
market_signals.observation: Meyer Werft Project Vision is the first credible large-scale fully electric cruise ship concept from a tier-1 builder.
market_signals.interpretation: Battery-electric is moving up the vessel size ladder faster than expected. If one cruise operator orders, it resets demand expectations entirely.

projects_30d.ess_scope: 40 MWh Dolphin NxtGen Power (70 MWh future-ready)

technology_bullets.title: Dolphin NxtGen Power confirmed on large ferry programme
technology_bullets.body: BC Ferries Summit Class specifies Dolphin NxtGen Power with future-ready 70 MWh architecture. Capacity upgrade without structural vessel modification is becoming a design expectation.

technology_bullets.title: Battery room replaces engine room — Meyer Werft Vision
technology_bullets.body: Project Vision eliminates the engine room entirely. No exhaust shaft or funnel needed. Fundamental vessel design shift, not just a propulsion swap.

competitive_snapshot.position: Dominant market leader. Largest pipeline in sector history.
competitive_snapshot.direction: Blue Whale NxtGen Q4 2026. Cruise segment via Meyer Werft.

competitive_snapshot.position: Fastest-growing challenger. Winning Nordic routes previously held by Corvus.
competitive_snapshot.direction: Austal partnership opens Pacific market. Large-scale LFP product watch.

regulatory_watch.update: Battery ESS safety work plan endorsed. Interim guidelines development underway. SDC 13 milestone May 2027.
regulatory_watch.impact: Suppliers must align documentation with anticipated guidelines. Class approvals from 2027 will reference these.

regulatory_watch.update: 70% CO2 allowance surrender in force 2026. 100% from 2027.
regulatory_watch.impact: 100% surrender from 2027 is the largest single commercial driver for hybrid retrofit enquiries.

takeaways.matters_now: The BC Ferries Summit Class future-ready 70 MWh architecture is the commercial signal of the week. Corvus is selling upgrade optionality baked into the vessel — operators can justify conservative initial capacity knowing full electric is pre-engineered. Expect this pattern to become standard on new hybrid ferry programmes within 18 months.
takeaways.watch_next: Whether Meyer Werft Project Vision attracts a cruise operator order before year-end is the single most consequential commercial question in the sector. Also watch IMO SDC 13 (May 2027) — treat the next 9 months as preparation time for interim guideline compliance documentation.
takeaways.means_for_integrators: EU ETS hitting 100% surrender in 2027 means commercial pressure is intensifying materially. The retrofit RFQ pipeline should be building now for H1 2027 delivery. Integrators with class-ready ESS documentation, LFP product lines, and crew training capability will be best positioned.
